operator.payload: If the same project field is selected more than once (for example, with both `--field Status` and `--field-id <Status-ID>`), should it appear once or as repeated table columns?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: `--field` and `--field-id` cannot be combined and must fail clearly. Repeating the same field within either one permitted flag form produces repeated columns in the requested order.

operator.payload: For multi-value fields such as labels, assignees, reviewers, and linked pull requests, should table cells use a comma-and-space-separated list of their human-readable names (and URLs for linked pull requests)?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Yes. Labels use label names; users use logins; reviewers use user logins and team names; linked pull requests use URLs. Join multiple values with `, ` in one cell.

Add repeatable `--field <name>` and repeatable `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. They are mutually exclusive: supplying both fails before any API requests with a clear flag-validation error. Repeating either permitted flag retains each requested occurrence and order, including duplicates, producing repeated columns.

For normal table output, retain the existing Type, Title, Number, Repository, and ID columns unchanged, then append one column per requested field. Each appended header uses the project’s canonical field name returned by GitHub, including when selected by ID. Resolve `--field` names case-insensitively and IDs exactly against `project.Fields.Nodes`, which is already returned by the ordinary ProjectItems request; do not issue a separate ProjectFields preflight request. Missing names and IDs fail with actionable available-field candidates; ambiguous case-insensitive names fail with matching IDs and guidance to use `--field-id`. Resolution completes before rendering so no partial or silently incorrect table is produced.

For every item, locate its value by resolved field ID. An unset value renders as an empty cell. Render returned field values as readable text: date/text/single-select values directly; numbers in ordinary decimal form; iterations and milestones by title; labels, users, reviewers, and linked pull requests as comma-and-space lists (label names, user logins, reviewer user logins/team names, and pull-request URLs respectively); repository fields as their returned URL. Unknown or unsupported value variants render as empty cells.

The selection flags apply only to table output. Combining either with `--format` fails clearly because formatted output is not a table and must not silently ignore a requested column. With no selection flags, text and formatted output behavior stays unchanged. Add command parsing, mutual-exclusion, resolution, value-rendering, table-order, duplicate-column, failure, formatted-output-conflict, and no-extra-preflight tests.
